To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The distribution of kidney centre depths in the sitting position is not symmetrical, and this distribution has a significant standard deviation (1.9 +/- 2.2 cm, mean +/- SD).
kidney position is not normally distributed in patients presenting for renograms, and that this distribution affects the accuracy of the renogram measurement of relative effective kidney plasma flow.
the position of the kidneys is variable and this affects the measurement of the relative uptake of Hippuran in renograms.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the measurement of the distribution of kidney positions in a sitting posture, the effect of this distribution on the measurement of renal function by 131-I hippuran renography and the effect of localizing techniques in the measurement of kidney position and function.
the effect of kidney position on the measurement of kidney function.
the development of new methods for the measurement of renal function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in a patient with a normal distribution of kidney centre position and normal renal function, the error in relative effective renal plasma flows calculated from probe renography would have a mean of zero, and a SD of 21 per cent.
the use of the probe renogram in the sitting posture for the measurement of relative function is subject to significant error.

, if no kidney localizing technique is used and if the kidneys are not symmetrically placed, then the measurement of relative function by 131-I probe renography will have an SD of 22 per cent, which is too large to be useful in clinical practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of kidney localizing techniques, in particular ultrasound scanning, is to be recommended.

the measurement of relative renal function by probe renography is subject to a considerable error in the absence of a kidney localizing technique, and that the use of such a technique is essential for the measurement of relative function.

, in the absence of kidney localizing techniques, the measurement of relative renal plasma flow by probe renography in a patient with a normal distribution of kidney positions is subject to a random error of 22 per cent in the measurement of relative function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the measurement of relative kidney function by renography is subject to a random error which is not negligible.
the measurement of effective renal plasma flow using 131-I Hippuric Acid probe renography is subject to a significant error in the absence of a kidney localization technique.
, in the sitting posture, kidney position has a significant effect on the accuracy of renography.
